html: The Pequonnock were an Algonquian-speaking people of the Connecticut shore of Long Island Sound, around present Bridgeport and the Pequonnock River. They are usually counted among the Paugussett peoples, with the Quinnipiac to the east. They farmed maize, fished and gathered shellfish. After the Pequot War of 1636 to 1638 English settlers moved into their land, and in 1659 a small reservation was set aside for them at Golden Hill in Bridgeport. Their descendants are part of the Golden Hill Paugussett, who still hold a small state reservation.
